correctness.rationale: Positive linear averaging admits exact binary-cut norm reduction. For any bistochastic image y in [0,1]^n of a k-cut, layer-cake proves k(n-k)-G(y)=int_0^1(m(t)-k)^2 dt; cyclic three-tap outputs have levels 0,1/3,2/3,1, giving the exact sum of squares for counts d,b,e. For a cut with at least two 1s and two 0s, cyclic boundary counts imply d-k>=2 and e-k<=-2, so deficit >=8/3, with equality for single runs. Singleton deficit is 2. Taking k maximizing k(n-k)=floor(n^2/4) proves gamma_n=1-8/[3 floor(n^2/4)] for n>=4, and n=3 rank-one constant map. n=4 exact complement of antipodal permutation gives all-real 1/3 equality. Two disjoint row supports for n>=6 prove oscillation coefficient 1. The all-n claim depends on the boundary lemma, not the finite enumeration.
